revision_note: Before candidate/final paired measurements: correct invalid benchmark overload idempotency keys, preserve partial failures, exclude health warmup, and clarify first-event metric. First baseline and original plan retained. Numeric budgets unchanged. Added bounded live dashboard HTTP queries, diagnostic only.
purpose: A reviewer and a second customer operate the local pilot while reading their streams. This is a bounded diagnostic, not a production capacity or reliability claim.
selection_basis: Two customers follows the demo. Budgets are user-visible responsiveness limits chosen before measurements; the preserved implementation is measured first and retained even if it misses them. No previous quantitative capacity baseline exists.
baseline: Preserved commit c0afb816d68fe2b3367c0457ffc271d163a0f793, exported into a fresh directory; no source checkout is modified.
candidate: Immutable integrated commit 87970608892a0d130a18f9c6bc31bdfcf0e9e471 exported into a fresh directory, with exact file hashes and archive receipt.

profile.processes: one ASGI service, one synthetic provider, clients on same host
profile.provider_profile: success, no injected delay except explicitly identified overload probe
profile.rate_limit_caveat: Accelerated diagnostic profile from the existing test harness. Default product rate is 60/minute and burst 20; this is not a default-profile capacity claim. A separate default-rate overload probe is included.

matrix.description: idempotent session-create command replay; HTTP acceptances do not imply unique effects
full proposal, exact prompt fetch, consent, committed completion; 40 unique effects per repetition and concurrency
40 unique effects with one live SSE reader per customer, health polling and reconnect catch-up after the first committed event
two non-reading sockets hold a pending run while an unrelated customer completes 12 operations; small traffic does not prove kernel-buffer saturation
hold four streams for one principal and expect typed 429 for the fifth; replay creates no provider effect
eight unapproved runs fill the configured active-run limit; ninth must be refused with no effect
fresh stack with default burst20/rate60; expect bounded typed 429 refusals
off/on/injected-failure optional recorder call; bounded capacity; separate microbenchmark, not whole-service instrumentation A/B
One excluded warmup then authenticated list/aggregate HTTP reads after 21 owned runs. Missing on preserved baseline is NOT_AVAILABLE, not a regression. Browser render time excluded.

budgets.scope: Idle, pilot at 1/2 customers, mixed streams and slow-consumer completion. Overload refusal timing is diagnostic. Budgets are not CI gates on shared hardware.

statistics.warmup: publish raw warmup; exclude from steady-state percentiles/throughput
statistics.small_sample: p95 is descriptive; 40 observations per repetition and correlated local runs cannot establish a stable production tail
statistics.clock: client monotonic elapsed only; consent-to-dispatch is client-observed dispatch_started delivery, including transport; no cross-process clock subtraction
statistics.first_event_definition: stream-open to first existing committed event delivered; proposal and prompt delivery already finished. This is replay-first-event latency, not request-to-commit latency or model time-to-first-token.
statistics.throughput: accepted consent HTTP requests and observed succeeded operations separately over the same measured phase wall interval
statistics.rss_cpu: sample service/provider ps RSS and cumulative CPU every 100ms; sampling may miss transient peaks
statistics.event_loop: health/live HTTP response is an external responsiveness proxy, not a direct event-loop lag instrument
statistics.db_growth: app/provider database plus WAL/SHM sizes before/after and sampled peak; local scratch deleted after final observation

limits: No model/provider paid calls, dependency installation, outbound network, UI or canonical source writes.
Hard correctness gates remain in the serving/evaluation suites; this harness independently counts synthetic provider effects but is not a replacement.
Preserve all first-run failures. Output directories are exclusive. Stop after one final run per source; repairs require a new output directory and explanation.
